about: Ilia: technical background, no formal finance training. He is designing an AI market insight app for stocks. The app reads news and research over weeks, links events into storylines (this happened, so that should follow; when the expected next event appears, the link is confirmed) and helps a human trader decide with less emotion. It is not high frequency trading and not based on price patterns. The goal is to beat the habits of casual retail traders, not to compete with funds. This review is about methods: what to actually trade when trading on news and events over days to weeks, how long to hold, what it returns after costs, and whether it still works. Screening rules. Keep: stocks in any country (US and Europe preferred), real market data, studies that report returns, holding periods or trading costs. Prefer: open full text (NBER, SSRN and arXiv versions count), samples that run past 2010, and applied journals such as the Financial Analysts Journal and the Journal of Portfolio Management. Drop (relevance 2 or less): technical analysis and chart patterns, high frequency and intraday trading, crypto, forex, options strategies, and pure theory without data.

themes.name: Events that make prices drift
themes.question: Which company events (earnings surprises, guidance and analyst revisions, recommendation changes, insider buying, buybacks, index additions, dividend initiations) are followed by prices that keep moving in the same direction, by how much, and for how many days or weeks?
queries: stock price reaction to news and no news
share repurchase announcements long run returns

themes.name: News spreading to linked companies
themes.question: When news hits one company, how and how slowly do the prices of linked companies (customers, suppliers, industry peers, firms sharing analysts or technology) follow, and can that delay be traded over days to weeks?
queries: supply chain information diffusion stock returns

themes.name: Text and attention signals
themes.question: Do signals built from text (news tone, novelty, changes in filings, earnings call language, language model readings) or from investor attention (searches, media coverage) predict stock returns over days to weeks, and how large and lasting is the effect?
queries: annual report text changes future returns
large language models news stock returns

themes.name: Already priced in or not
themes.question: How much of a news event is priced on the day it appears versus over the following days and weeks, when do prices underreact or overreact, and what (distraction, timing, informed trading beforehand) decides which?
queries: speed of price adjustment to news
anomaly returns on news and earnings days

themes.name: Does it still work
themes.question: Do news and event based return patterns survive trading costs, publication, recent years and a filter that removes tiny illiquid stocks, and how much of the reported return is left?
queries: decline of post earnings announcement drift
anomalies in small and microcap stocks

themes.name: From signal to trade
themes.question: Once a signal fires, what does the evidence say about when to enter, how long to hold, when to exit, how much to put in each position, how many positions to hold, and what trading costs do to a retail sized account?

themes.name: Skill or luck
themes.question: How can a trader tell whether good results come from skill or luck, how long a track record is needed, how should backtests be corrected for testing many ideas, and do individual investors learn from their own trading?
queries: multiple testing cross section of expected returns
